NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The proposal is a **pure operating-point retuning** of the reactor temperature setpoint and a defined **procedure change** to the oleum feed rate ramp-up, executing the permitted "temperature setpoint retuning" and "concentration procedure only" axes. Standard practice operates at a fixed 100 °C with a standard ramp; this intervention lowers the steady-state operating temperature to 85 °C and extends the ramp-up duration by 100% to reduce peak local exotherm rates and acid concentration transients that drive liner corrosion. The adjacent-technique clearance is that standard practice uses a "steady-state operation" class, while this intervention uses a "derated steady-state + extended ramp" class; the departure is the **operating point selection** (lower temperature) and the **schedule** (extended ramp) applied to existing controls.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing relation for corrosion rate $r$ in this system is Arrhenius-type: $r = A e^{-E_a/RT}$, where $E_a$ is the activation energy for liner degradation (typically 50–80 kJ/mol for high-temperature acid service). Reducing temperature $T$ from 373 K (100 °C) to 358 K (85 °C) reduces $r$ by a factor of $e^{(E_a/R)(1/358 - 1/373)} \approx 2.5–4$. Additionally, the corrosion integral over the duty cycle $I = \int r(t) dt$ is minimized by lowering the baseline $r$ and extending the ramp-up time $\Delta t_{ramp}$, which reduces the peak instantaneous acid concentration transient $C_{acid,peak}$, a known driver of localized pitting.

The extended ramp moves peak acid concentration transient DOWN, further reducing localized damage integral.
